x: How well Tony Binda has fitted into the Youths team, he has only been with us a few weeks but has already won the hearts of his team mates by some really gritty running, both in training and races.

Peter's efforts have induced others to follow suit and climb to the standards set by Bill Curtin, so instead of having a solitary spearhead and a group of supporting runners down the field we now have Curtin, Carton and John Stow with little separating them and Tony Binda and Les Harris determined to close that gap.

John Stowe was only 120 yards further back with Tony Binda a similar distance behind John, but closing fast. Our Press Honorary Secretary, Don Maclean, was an interested spectator as he was a winner of this race in the early 1950's.
One who was far from 'out' was Tony Binda whose slight frame skimmed over the muddy surface of the closing stages faster, probably, than any of the field.
Walton's Francis pipped Peter Carton again for third place and Tony Binda ran through strongly to secure 11th place, just two places ahead of Vic Butcher who closed in our scoring four.
TONY BINDA takes over from JOHN STOWE for the third stage of the Mitcham Young Athletes Relay at Morden Park.

With Carton and Curtin grimly hanging on to their places around the twenty mark, John Stowe going well in the early sixties and Tony Binda only another twenty places back, a count at two miles placed us second, yes second.

Peter's two rivals, John Stow and Bill Curtin steered clear and pooled their resources in the 3,000 metres, Tony Binda also toned up. John found himself up against his Surrey County victor Ford(Aldershot F.D.) and Julian Goater (Shaftesbury) who is coached by the man who took Dave Bedford through to the Senior ranks.
ABOVE: Martin Bloice wins the Youth 400 metres by a whisker. LEFT: Tony Binda (right) wins his first County vest---for walking! He was 4th in the Junior 'A' string race.

Twenty five starters toed the line, the same number as last year, and there was much speculation as to how newcomers like Peter Carton and Tony Binda would fare, and as to how much fitness was tucked away in that old campaigner Pat Newell.
The terrible trio of this season's Surrey League, youths and boys: - Peter Carton happy, Bill Curtin a trifle bored, and Tony Binda apparently wondering when the race is going to start.

Tireless Tony Binda runs week in week out without a trace of fatigue, so it seems. Although not brilliant on the track, he is developing into a road and cross-country specialist in the Gerry North/Bert Foster mould.
Tony Binda came 50th, John Stow 175th and Pat Breslin 197th The whole team except Mark appeared jaded - Bill although physically below par lacked nothing in determination - to beat Peter.
Tony Binda (25) and Colin Pearson locked in battle in the Wimbledon Cup. For the winner, see the sparkling report elsewhere in this issue. - Photo: Ron Lin[illegible]tead

Three Belgrave runners finished in the Country's scoring four - Bill Curtin coming home tenth in 18m. 58s. - some 32s. behind the winner- while Peter Carton was one place further back in 18m. 59s., and Tony Binda was the third Surrey man, with 26th place in 19m. 32s.

Trials sometimes do something to sort out selection problems, but on this occasion the most important performance was put up by Guy Monnet, whose 15m. 06s. - slightly faster than the times returned by Tony Fairclough and Tony Binda - must have caused some headaches.
Young Tony Binda had an unenviable task in his first race of this calibre - but he did well to hold his position and clock 15m. 52s. on the eighth stage.

Trevor Hart showed some improved form, in third place, while youths Bill Curtin, Peter Carton, Tony Binda and John Stow added to their growing reputations with fourth, sixth, seventh and twelfth, respectively.

Continuing their habit of swapping the first three places to deliberately thwart the judges and produce a tie for the trophy awarded to the best individual of the series, Tony Binda, Peter Carton, and Bill Curtin trotted home in that order to lead the field in.

Although this event was open to runners up to the age of 20, we scored a fine win with an all youth quartet. John Stow took the first stage and handed over to Tony Binda in 4th place recording 9m 2s. Tony clocked 8m 44s to move into 2nd position.
Recording 18m.53secs., Peter had 29 secs in hand over Tony Binda, who in turn was 17 secs up on Bill Curtin. John Stow, rapidly coming back to form was sixth.
Tony Binda was second, half a minute in arrears, and third was John Stow. Mark Clancy filled fourth spot with injury plagued Pat Breslin in fifth position.

A solid performance by our junior team, of Peter Carton (4th), Tony Binda (12th), Bill Curtin (17th) and John Stow (32nd) gave them a praiseworthy third - not all that far behind the winners, Thames Valley.

In the junior race, our famous four were 11th, with Peter Carton, who just missed a junior international,vest getting good support for his 10th place from Tony Binda (58th), Bill Curtin (109th) and John Stow (111th), and Mark Clancy again poised to fill any breach that should appear.

However, whatever else may transpire this is no time to relax our efforts for once again we have the unfortunate task of saying good-bye (one that seems to happen all too often for us) to two of our most promising younger stars namely, Tony Binda and Tony Brien.

That popular runner Tony Binda left these shores to return to sunny Jamaica, his birthplace, and rejoin his parents now living in Kingston. He will be sorely missed for his cheeky wit and of course his excellent running.

TONY BRIEN, who was our first man home in last year's National, is now resident at Kansas University, U.S.A., TONY BINDA, a fast improving Junior with tremendous potential has returned to the West Indies just as he was beginning to show the form to get amongst our senior scorers, and JOHN PHELAN is…
John Phelan wins Club 7 mile cross country championship from Laurie O'Hara and Tony Binda. Junior Championship held on same day won by Reg Hopkins.
A special presentation in the form of a silver Elizabethan dish, inscribed with an English Rose, was made after the race to Tony Binda on the eve of his departure from the Belgrave fold.
What a pity that our once unbeatable team of Tony Binda, Bill Curtin and John Stow , backing up Peter if not battling with him for individual honours, has now disintegrated.

"Come back Tony Binda!" is the first thought, for Tony had already shown that he was about to break through and provide Peter with close support before his move to the West Indies wrecked the possibility.
Tony Binda hands over to Bruce Taylor at Crystal Palace

Pat O'Connor, making a welcome and well-timed recovery from injury, recorded second fastest time of the day behind Leo Coy and in front of the in-form John Jackson ("I don't really like these sprint races") and our new Captain Tony Binda ("It's too cold to run here").

Unfortunately he had no immediate back-up over the short, hilly five mile course until Simon Holmes in 87th place and Tony Binda in 93rd. There was another long gap until Tom Dowdall closed in the 'A' team in 189th.

The second group of Gerry North, Lionel Mann, Colin Pearson and Simon Holmes were always falling back and the experience and fitness of Pat O'Connor and Tony Binda brought them through well at the end.

Tony Binda was forced to stop and walk on the second lap with bad cramp in the stomach and Steve Williams, after a promising return in the '10', was forced to retire with the same diaphragm trouble that has dogged him since the summer.
With a full team we could have been in the medals. 'A' Team: S.Williamson 13.39; S.Holmes 13.38; A.Binda 13.49; L.Coy 14.26.

Also notable were Tony Binda's return to form, Bob Smith's business like return to the road running scene as well as our younger stars, Mark Waller and Mark Sinclair making their presence felt in senior company with first class times for their ages.

Tony Binda, however, showed some improvement on his rather mediocre form of late by scoring an all too infrequent victory over Jim Rimmer and we also had a small consolation in that this year we did at least field a full team of nine runners!!

Another 'old' Belgravian met at the National Junior League was Tony Binda, whose nephew sprints for Reading AC. Tony reckons he is hoping to make a comeback - we'll see.
